research_question_and_methods.justification: objective_and_hypothesis: This matches the score_2 description: the objective is clear and method-linked—identifying the unknown YFV receptor through an overexpression screen—but the paper does not state a distinct, prospective hypothesis before presenting LRP8 as the screen result. | public_health_relevance: This matches the score_3 description because yellow fever is presented as a substantial current public-health threat and the paper explicitly relates the work to recognized recent outbreaks in multiple countries. | study_design_rigor: This matches the score_3 description: the paper provides detailed protocols for the ORFeome screen, virus production, entry assays, knockout/rescue experiments, BLI, primary hepatocyte studies, mosquito knockdown, and mouse models. Results are validated with orthogonal methods across Figures 1–6, and scRNA-seq raw data are deposited under GSA-Human accession HRA013453.

objective_and_hypothesis.justification: This matches the score_2 description: the objective is clear and method-linked—identifying the unknown YFV receptor through an overexpression screen—but the paper does not state a distinct, prospective hypothesis before presenting LRP8 as the screen result.
objective_and_hypothesis.quote: To uncover the long‑sought YFV receptor, we applied a barcoded ORFeome library

public_health_relevance.justification: This matches the score_3 description because yellow fever is presented as a substantial current public-health threat and the paper explicitly relates the work to recognized recent outbreaks in multiple countries.
public_health_relevance.quote: Recent outbreaks occurred in Brazil, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Angola, Uganda, and Nigeria, with spillover cases in Asia

study_design_rigor.justification: This matches the score_3 description: the paper provides detailed protocols for the ORFeome screen, virus production, entry assays, knockout/rescue experiments, BLI, primary hepatocyte studies, mosquito knockdown, and mouse models. Results are validated with orthogonal methods across Figures 1–6, and scRNA-seq raw data are deposited under GSA-Human accession HRA013453.
study_design_rigor.quote: Unless otherwise specified, experiments were repeated at least three times.

results_and_conclusion.justification: Although the manuscript contains extensive figures and several orthogonal validations, it meets the score_1 description because its stated ZIKV-specificity conclusion is directly contradicted by Figure 6c: one dsVLDLR mosquito condition shows a statistically significant 1.69-fold ZIKV difference (p=0.006), despite the text claiming no effect on ZIKV infection. This is a specific reported data point inconsistent with the paper's stated conclusion, rather than merely unclear statistical reporting.
results_and_conclusion.quote: this block was specific to YFV and had no effect on Zika virus infection

references.justification: The references provide relevant coverage of yellow-fever epidemiology, vaccine attenuation, flavivirus entry, LDLR-family receptors, alphavirus receptor biology, screening methods, and animal models. They include foundational and recent peer-reviewed sources in high-quality journals, alongside appropriate authoritative and methodological sources such as the WHO fact sheet and Fields Virology; no clearly unrelated reference was identified.
references.quote: Clark, L. E. et al. VLDLR and ApoER2 are receptors for multiple alphaviruses.
